title: OCIA Session I: The Journey of Faith
requirements: Explore the four stages of OCIA, the universal search for God, Divine Revelation, and the meaning of faith.

sections.title: 1. What is OCIA?
sections.content: The Order of Christian Initiation of Adults is not a mere academic course, but a gradual spiritual journey into full communion with the Catholic Church. It is structured in four distinct stages:

stages.description: Deeper study, spiritual growth, and formation.
Deepening your understanding of the sacraments after Easter.

sections.title: 2. The Universal Search
sections.content: Every human being is born with a "God-shaped vacuum" in their heart. We have an built-in, unquenchable desire for perfect truth, beauty, goodness, and love.

points.author: St. Augustine
points.quote: You have made us for yourself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.

points: We can look at the order of creation and the voice of our moral conscience to reasonably deduce that God exists.
However, human reason alone cannot give us an intimate, saving relationship with God. For that, we need Him to reveal Himself.

sections.title: 3. God’s Response: Divine Revelation
sections.content: God did not stay hidden or silent. Out of pure love, He stepped into human history to show us Who He is:
points: He made Covenants with Abraham, Moses, and the people of Israel.
He spoke fully and definitively by becoming man in Jesus Christ.
Today, this revelation reaches us through the Word of God, preserved in Sacred Scripture (the Bible) and Sacred Tradition (the living teaching of the Church).

sections.title: 4. What is Faith?
sections.content: Faith is our personal response to God’s invitation. It is a supernatural gift from God that requires our free human cooperation.

aspects.description: Surrendering yourself completely to a loving relationship with God.
Accepting the objective truths God has revealed (found in the Creed).
They are two wings on which the human spirit rises. The Catholic Church teaches they never contradict; instead, they complement and elevate one another.

catechism_reading.title: Catechism (CCC) Reading
catechism_reading.description: To dive deeper into tonight's topic, read these sections in your Catechism this week:

readings.summary: Knowing God through reason and creation.
The true meaning and act of faith.

questions: Where in your life have you felt the "restlessness" that St. Augustine talks about?
Looking back at your life's path, how do you see God gently drawing you toward this training?

scriptural_foundations.title: Paul’s Speech at the Areopagus
scriptural_foundations.summary: Explains how God created humans to seek Him, grope for Him, and find Him, noting that "in Him we live and move and have our being."

scriptural_foundations.title: Longing for God
scriptural_foundations.summary: The classic, beautiful cry of the soul searching for its Creator: "As the deer longs for streams of water, so my soul longs for you, O God."

scriptural_foundations.title: The Definition of Faith
scriptural_foundations.summary: Explains that "faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen" and details why faith pleases God.

scriptural_foundations.title: Seeking with the Heart
scriptural_foundations.summary: A comforting reminder of God’s active pursuit of us: "When you look for me, you will find me. Yes, when you seek me with all your heart."
